Henna on the forearm stains lighter than on the palm because the skin is thinner. Arm designs are easier to apply on someone else than on yourself, especially past the wrist. This is a detailed pattern usually done by an experienced artist; allow plenty of time and work in small sections.

image.alt: Indonesian Leaf Trail mehndi design for arm — luxurious henna pattern

faq.q: Should I do a patch test before applying mehndi?
faq.a: Yes. Apply a small amount of the paste to the inner arm and wait 24 hours, especially if you have sensitive skin or are using a new cone.

faq.q: How long does a mehndi stain last?
faq.a: A natural henna stain usually lasts one to three weeks. It fades faster on areas that are washed or rubbed often, such as the hands.

faq.q: How long should I leave the mehndi paste on?
faq.a: Keep the paste on for at least four to six hours. Many people leave it overnight for a darker stain.

Moroccan henna is distinctive for its bold geometric patterns that differ significantly from South Asian floral styles. In Berber tradition, specific geometric henna symbols carry protective meanings against the evil eye.

Application tips: Moroccan designs use tape or stencils for clean geometric lines — a technique called 'henna bil scotch'. Start with the structural grid pattern before filling in individual geometric cells.

image.alt: Indonesian Bell Garland mehndi design for arm — graceful henna pattern

faq.q: What makes Moroccan henna different?
faq.a: Moroccan henna features bold geometric and tribal patterns derived from Berber traditions, unlike the floral styles of Arabic and Indian henna.

faq.q: Do Moroccan henna designs have meanings?
faq.a: Yes, many Berber geometric symbols carry specific meanings — diamonds represent femininity, triangles provide protection, and the hamsa wards off the evil eye.

faq.q: Is Moroccan henna paste different?
faq.a: Moroccan henna paste is known for being exceptionally pure and fine. Fez and Marrakech are famous for producing high-quality henna powder.
